clips.caption:
You're not a body having occasional spiritual moments. It's the other way around.

You're a spiritual being, temporarily having a human experience. And the reason you're here isn't to accumulate things - it's to create. Watch a child at the beach build a sandcastle, and the second it's finished, they knock it down. The joy was never in having it. It was entirely in building it.

That's not a metaphor for children. That's what you're actually built to do.

Most people walk around disassociated from themselves, and they can't even name what's missing.

Not liking who they are. Not comfortable in their own skin. Always reaching for something they can't describe, let alone locate. That's not a small percentage of people struggling - that's the majority.

The process of getting out of that isn't instant, and it may not even finish in this lifetime. But there's one thing that moves it faster than almost anything else.

clips.caption:
There's a line from an old book that sounds too simple to work: greet everyone you meet with love in your heart, and silently say to them, "I love you."

You don't say it out loud. You don't act differently. You just hold it internally, even for someone who hasn't earned it yet. If love feels like too much, compassion works too - simply deciding that this person, like you, has a right to be happy.

Say it enough times and the one it ends up changing is you.

Walk into a dark basement and see something coiled in the corner, and your whole body reacts - it's a snake.

Turn the light on and look again. It was always a rope. Nothing in the room changed. Only what you could see changed.

That's what enlightenment actually means - not a new power, just enough light to see what was already there the whole time: that you're one with everything, that looking inward finds more than looking outward ever did. The kingdom was never far away. You just needed the light on.
